learn.title: How to Test Your Agents on Real Tasks With Harbor - Xander Song, Arize AI
learn.headline: Free Harbor tool tests agents on realistic tasks with checks and rewards.
learn.reason: Shows how to evaluate agents with verifiers and trial runs, a core eval skill you're learning.

card.headline: A free open source tool tests AI agents on realistic tasks
card.gist: Harbor gives an AI agent, a program where an AI takes steps alone, a realistic task. Each test runs in a sealed-off workspace, and a checker then decides if the task succeeded.
card.picture: Think of testing an ETL job in a separate staging database. You load real data, run the job, then run a check query on the output. Harbor does this for an AI agent.
card.why_you: When you change a prompt, you can rerun the same tasks and compare results. The talk shows one team doing this for a prompt change.
card.remember: Test agent changes on the same real tasks, then compare.
card.term_meaning: A check that runs after the agent finishes and scores whether the task succeeded.
card.say_it: I test agents on realistic tasks in isolated sandboxes, with verifiers that work like black-box integration tests.
card.follow_up_why: Because a pass or fail on real tasks is evidence, while a quick look is only a feeling.
card.reality_check: This is a talk by an Arize AI engineer about Harbor; Harbor is open source.
card.try_it: Watch the chapter at 07:58 and write down the task, the environment and the verifier.

learn.title: Can Your AI Analyst Keep a Secret? - Aaron Linsky, Bridgewater & Nikhil Benesch, turbopuffer
learn.headline: Vector search with permissions: why filtering before or after search matters.
learn.reason: Explains pre-filter, post-filter and native filtering trade-offs, which RAG interviews ask about.

card.headline: How an AI analyst searches private documents without leaking them
card.gist: An AI analyst at Bridgewater searches private emails, memos and research notes. Each document has its own access rules, and at 100 million documents their first search setup broke.
card.picture: Imagine a query that returns the top ten matches, then hides rows the user may not see. You may be left with only two rows. The fix applies the access rule while searching, so all ten results are allowed.
card.why_you: You are learning to build AI search over documents. Real company documents always come with rules about who may see them.
card.remember: Apply access rules during the search, not after it.
card.term_meaning: Applying filters, such as permissions, inside the vector index search itself, not before or after it.
card.say_it: For permissioned RAG, post-filtering loses recall and pre-filtering is too slow, so I'd filter inside the index.
card.follow_up_why: Because filtering after the search can remove most top results, so good matches go missing.
card.reality_check: The speed figures come from turbopuffer's CTO, a vendor, not from an independent test.
card.try_it: In pandas, take the top 10 rows by score, then filter by a team column. Count rows left.
